newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian budget moves into surplus in May.
newsitem.headline: Canadian budget moves into surplus in May.

text.p: Canada's federal budget moved into surplus in May for the first time this year, to C$1.37 billion, compared with a C$582 million deficit a year earlier, the Finance Department said on Friday.

It was the first surplus since a rare C$2.19 billion surplus recorded in December, but the Finance Department said some of the gains in May would not be repeated or would be reversed later in the year.
"Caution should be exercised in extrapolating the monthly results to gain an assessment of the possible outcome for the (fiscal) year as a whole," it said.

For example, it said, the current increase in employment insurance premiums -- whose collection was front-loaded to the first half of the year -- will be reversed by the end of the year. Nonetheless, those premiums rose by only C$336 million between May 1996 and May 1997, accounting for only a fraction of the C$1.95 billion overall budget improvement for May.
For the first two months of the fiscal year, April and May, the deficit shrank to C$2.04 billion from C$4.64 billion a year earlier.
(Note: Positive numbers indicate net source of funds. Negative numbers indicate net requirement for funds.)
